home-06.rationale: Indonesian mesin cuci and Malaysian mesin basuh are ordinary terms for a washing machine. The forms differ in the verb used and create a useful national contrast.

concerns: Indonesian pel and Malaysian mop are different forms but do not present a genuine national contrast for this sense; the pairing is an artificial synonym.
material_concerns: It does not provide a useful Indonesian–Malaysian recall contrast.
home-07.rationale: The Indonesian form pel and Malaysian form mop both refer to a cleaning tool for washing floors. Because the forms differ, the relation is not same; the plausible defect is artificial-synonym.

concerns: Malaysian sikat rambut can be somewhat broader than a toothed comb and may also refer to a hairbrush.
home-08.rationale: Indonesian sisir and Malaysian sikat rambut are ordinary terms that can naturally denote a comb used for arranging hair. They are unrelated word forms and provide a useful contrast, though sikat rambut has some brush-related breadth.

home-09.rationale: Indonesian sikat gigi and Malaysian berus gigi are ordinary, natural terms for a toothbrush. The lexical contrast is clear and useful.

concerns: Wajan is also understood elsewhere in the Malay-Indonesian region, but it is an ordinary Indonesian term; kuali is the ordinary Malaysian term.
home-10.rationale: Indonesian wajan and Malaysian kuali naturally express the same everyday sense of a shallow pan used for frying. They are unrelated forms and teach a useful national vocabulary contrast.
